title: Mid
body:
Pros
Nice Layout
Simple with colour coding

Cons
High price point
Limited functions with reminders i.e. no ability to set reminders for specific days of the week. You are limited to selecting only everyday, once a week, once a month. I simply want to remind myself to make a packed lunch for the days I work in the office and I only work in the office 3 days but I can either set the habit reminder everyday or not at all. It will not let me pick specific days to recur each week. Very frustrating to expect to keep me paying more than the discounted price next year. 

I definitely will be setting a reminder on a different app so I cancel the subscription before I am charged $60 more in 2025, if the app doesn’t improve. Though I probably will quit anyways as it just doesn’t make sense to pay more than $10 on any app. Since when did apps become so expensive?

title: Shameful and predatory development practices
body:
Having bought the premium version of the app, I expect to be able to use the premium features perpetually. Instead the developer has shifted to an annual subscription model, and my previously bought premium version is nullified.

I understand stand the shift to a subscription model from a business perspective, however it is a predatory and unfaithful to your early supporters to revoke access to features they bought outright.

Another app called Strong (workout app) had a similar shift of business model, and honoured people who previously purchased the premium version while allowing new customers on to the subscription model. You should look to them for an example of integrity.

The app itself is decent, but I would not suggest that anyone support these developers given the number of alternative habit apps out there.

The subscription pop up is nauseating, not to mention its countdown timer pressuring payment auto renews after expiring. Big integrity drop. I’ve reached out to the developer without response so far. Previously they were prompt to respond. Really hoping will receive contact soon notifying of a bug fix and taking on board the feedback thoughtfully. Habit building requires daily consistency, app muck ups at this scale negatively impact habit flows. Considering looking for another option to replace this one if there isn’t communication working the issues through soon

Edit: the developer seems to have addressed a lot of the issues that came up earlier this year and the app is operating reasonably well again so I’ve modified my star rating.

title: The developer owes us all an explanation
body:
This app now requires a SUBSCRIPTION even if you have PREVIOUSLY PURCHASED the app. 

Yes, it seems that after a single quiet update the premium version of this app has changed from a one-off purchase to a subscription, and now my previous premium purchase is now void. I have tried the Restore Purchase function to no avail. 

I have lost access to the widget and dark mode functionality I was promised, and now Habit aggressively advertises its new premium subscription whenever I open it - advertising the features that I already paid for and have been using for weeks. 

Developer, please tell us this is a bug and not a deliberate trick. It would be very convenient for you if the Restore Purchase function was bugged for several days, wouldn’t it? I imagine a lot of confused users have already transitioned over to the subscription, having forgotten that they already paid for premium. I very nearly did. 

I urge anyone considering using this app to wait for an explanation from the developer. You cannot trust them with your money or data until then.

title: I love it

author: anna bü

title: Great habit maker!
body: Great, free app. Love the pastel colours and user interface. Fantastic ability to see when habits were completed in the past using a month-by-month view. Not sure how the percentages work for habits that aren’t daily... mine seem to be lower than expected. Overall, excellent app, helping me achieve a better lifestyle. Waiting for the Apple Watch  version... pretty please.

body: Would like if it told me the number of consecutive days I’d checked off but overall a very nice app.

title: Very good
body:
It would be nice to see the success rate percentage based on how many times you’ve chosen to complete a habit. For example, I’ve made a habit where I go to the gym three times a week which I have been completing, but my percentage is still low compared to the habits I tick off every day. 

Otherwise a cool app. Looks great and easy to use!

author: RSLJ4

title: Thank you
body:
Your commitment to giving free users an unlimited number of habits is incredibly admirable. This is what puts you above the countless other habit trackers in the App Store and why I’m giving you five stars. 

For me personally, I would prefer to see a 7 day layout rather than 5 days so I can have an easy weekly overview but I can understand if the aesthetic doesn’t allow for it. If I could have this one option I would be completely sold onto premium.

Regardless, a very nicely designed app. Kudos!
